subject: Request: AWS Marketplace concession & non-standard commission split for BrightLeaf
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: AWS Marketplace concession & non-standard commission split for BrightLeaf

Team —

Following the demo and pricing review with BrightLeaf, they’re asking for a private AWS Marketplace listing with two non-standard items that require executive clearance: a) 35% rev-share for the first 12 months (we typically cap at 25% for similar ARR profiles), and b) Net90 invoice terms for the commit portion tied to their finance approval window.

Deal summary: BrightLeaf would commit $420k ARR on a 12-month private offer, with an initial onboarding credit of $30k we offered to offset migration risk. They want the higher rev-share because they’re asking for a co-marketing credit and extended listing exposure in the AWS storefront.

Why I’m escalating: Deal Desk flagged this as outside the standard commission and payment cadence. Legal also called out a bespoke reporting cadence and a requirement for invoice-level audit logs to comply with their vendor governance.

Requested approvals:
- Executive approval to allow a 35% rev-share for months 0–12 (reverts to 20% thereafter)
- Approval for Net90 on committed invoices only (consumable usage billing remains Net30)
- Permission to accept BrightLeaf’s audit clause subject to legal review (attached draft)

Attachments: BrightLeaf_MA_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal), revshare-calculation-sheet.xlsx (impact model)

Next steps I propose: If we get a provisional go/no-go from finance/legal today we can lock the private offer and share countersigned terms by EOD Tuesday. Karthik will coordinate the procurement questions.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--

From: Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Marketplace concession & non-standard commission split for BrightLeaf

Ben and Karthik —

Reviewed the numbers and legal asks. Summary of Deal Desk review:
- Rev-share: 35% for year 1 materially increases CAC-adjusted payback and commission liabilities. We can consider a timebound elevation but need finance & revenue ops signoff.
- Payment terms: Net90 on committed invoice is a cashflow risk; recommend Net45 conditioned on an approved billing guarantee or a purchase order.
- Audit clause: Legal wants the clause narrowed to attendance of on-site audit once per year and limits on data scope.

We’ll need:
1) Finance (Laure n) to confirm ability to accept Net45 conditionals or approve Net90 with credit support.
2) Revenue Ops (Marissa) to confirm commission treatment and clawback mechanics.
3) Legal (Markus) to suggest narrowed audit language and confirm acceptable SLAs for invoice-level logs.

If internal approvals align, Deal Desk can issue a provisional private offer SKU with the elevated rev-share capped to the first 12 months and a cliff at month 13.

Marking for executive review — looping Lauren and Markus for fast turnaround.

-- Deal Desk

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T18:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Marketplace concession & non-standard commission split for BrightLeaf

Ben / team —

Thanks for the clear summary. I ran the impact model and here are finance’s guardrails:

- We can approve a temporary 35% rev-share for months 0–12 only if BrightLeaf agrees to an upfront partial prepayment or an irrevocable PO that covers at least 60% of the committed ARR within 30 days. Without that, Net90 is unacceptable.
- If the PO/partial prepayment is provided, finance will accept Net60 on committed invoices (not Net90), with usage billing on Net30.
- We need a 12-month clawback clause for partner credits and co-marketing reimbursements tied to revenue recognition to be documented in the contract.

Marissa, please confirm whether the proposed clawback mechanics are implementable in commission tooling and whether the elevated rev-share can be split across front-loaded commission (to sales) with holdbacks.

If legal (Markus) can tidy the audit clause and legal agree that the PO suffices as payment assurance, I’m provisionally OK to move forward. Final approval will need one signature from Revenue Head (Marissa) + CFO (Lauren).

I’ll wait for confirmation on PO/prepay or an alternative credit instrument.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: AWS Marketplace concession & non-standard commission split for BrightLeaf

Team —

I reviewed BrightLeaf’s proposed audit and the attached contract draft. Legal redline highlights:
1) Audit: narrowed to one annual audit, by a mutually agreed third party, limited to billing and invoice records related to the private offer; no access to production data or internal logs beyond invoice/audit trails.
2) PO / Prepay: acceptable as payment assurance; propose an escrow arrangement (we use third-party escrow) for amounts > $100k to mitigate collection risk.
3) Clawback: standard 12-month clawback language acceptable; recommend clarified triggers (refunds, failed revenue recognition, material breaches).

I will attach a clean redline and send to BrightLeaf procurement with the requested PO/escrow language. If finance confirms Net60 with PO or escrow, legal is okay with the timebound rev-share elevation under the above constraints.

Attached: redline_BrightLeaf_audit_clause.pdf (stub)

Markus Klein
General Counsel
Redwood Inference

--
